claim_boundary: This is a synthetic source-declared mechanical linear two-law intervention proof, not physical measured causal identification, real actuator, safety approval, or sensor calibration.
question: Can a precommitted active input distinguish two linear mechanisms for all unknown shared initial states despite passive observational equivalence and bounded per-model output error?
null_hypothesis: Passive readings or a one-tick-late pulse cannot force any nonzero separating residual, and any candidate with an unknown-state confound in the output difference must abstain.
selection_rule: Among exactly certified all-law-pair separating inputs, choose least nonzero actions, then minimum declared cost, then source order. Refuse entire search when any pair remains structurally ambiguous or its exact bounded-noise witness does not clear the margin.
proof: For pair models with common unknown x0, output delta = Delta O x0 + Delta b. Guaranteed nonzero under all x0 iff Delta b is not in colspace Delta O. A rational left-null witness w obeying w.T Delta O=0 and w.T Delta b != 0 certifies it. Against separate measurement L2 error <= epsilon, |w.T Delta b| > 2 epsilon ||w|| guarantees separation. If witness cannot clear declared error radius, abstain; do not claim impossibility.
